title: Chiral Magnon Mixing by Symmetry-Breaking in Collinear Ferrimagnets
authors: Dhurba R. Jaishi, Tyler J. Slade, S. X. M. Riberolles, Bing Li, Tianxiong Han, D. M. Pajerowski, D. L. Abernathy, Barry Winn, Melissa Graves-Brook, B. G. Ueland, R. J. McQueeney
abstract: Magnons in ferromagnets possess spin angular momentum defined by right-handed precession of the moment around the magnetization direction. In antiferromagnets with no net magnetization, left-and right-handed magnons are degenerate in the absence of an applied field. Ferrimagnets possess uncompensated magnetic sublattices, which should natively possess right-and left-handed magnons where their energy is split by the internal molecular field. Here, we show that RMn6Sn6 (R = Tb, Er) ferrimagnets possess right and left-handed magnon bands that cross at finite momentum (k) within the basal plane, defining modes with opposite dynamical chirality. Depending on the symmetry of the ferrimagnetic order, which may be manipulated by varying the rare-earth magnetic anisotropy or with applied field, the band crossing may remain a nodal line or may be gapped. The gapped modes contain hybridized chiral excitations whose chirality becomes k-dependent.
summary: This work explores how broken symmetries in ferrimagnets, specifically $	ext{RMn}_6	ext{Sn}_6$, induce mixing between right- and left-handed magnons. By combining theoretical modeling with polarized neutron scattering experiments, the authors demonstrate that anisotropy can cause a measurable reversal of magnon chirality within a single energy band. This highlights magnetic symmetry as a key control knob for manipulating quantum spin excitations.
main_problem: The study investigates chiral magnon mixing induced by symmetry-breaking mechanisms within collinear ferrimagnetic materials.
main_result: The research demonstrates that in $	ext{ErMn}_6	ext{Sn}_6$, magnetic anisotropy breaks the $U(1)$ symmetry, causing right- and left-handed magnons to hybridize, leading to a measurable reversal of chirality within a single magnon band as momentum changes.
method: The study combines theoretical calculations using linear spin-wave theory with experimental measurements from polarized inelastic neutron scattering (INS).
model_or_system: The system is the $	ext{RMn}_6	ext{Sn}_6$ kagome ferrimagnet. The physics is modeled via a Hamiltonian incorporating exchange interactions ($H_{	ext{ex}}$) and magnetic anisotropy ($H_{	ext{aniso}}$), which dictates the symmetry of the spin dynamics.
key_observables: Chiral scattering cross-section ($\sigma_{	ext{ch}}$) measured via polarized INS, magnon energy/momentum dispersion, and the degree of hybridization gap opening.
important_parameters: Rare-earth element (R = Tb, Er), applied magnetic field strength, and anisotropy parameters derived from CEF calculations ($B_m^l$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on linear spin-wave theory approximations. Some measurements involve integrating over transverse directions in the Brillouin zone.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structures, unpolarized/chiral INS spectra for both $	ext{TbMn}_6	ext{Sn}_6$ and $	ext{ErMn}_6	ext{Sn}_6$, and theoretical calculations showing how chirality changes near mode crossings due to symmetry breaking.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the background on magnon chirality in ferrimagnets, details the experimental setup using polarized INS, develops the spin-wave Hamiltonian incorporating anisotropy, presents results comparing $	ext{Tb}$ (uniaxial) and $	ext{Er}$ (planar) systems, and concludes by discussing the role of symmetry breaking in inducing chiral mixing.
why_interesting: The mechanism linking crystal symmetry breaking (anisotropy) to the hybridization and reversal of magnon chirality is a rich topic relevant to topological spin textures and emergent quantum phenomena in magnetic materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Chiral magnons in Tb166 and Er166. (a) Uniaxial ferrimagnetic structure of Tb166. (b) Planar ferrimagnetic structure of Er166. (c), (d) Unpolarized INS measurement of the magnon dispersions of Tb166 and Er166, respectively. For Tb166, measurements were performed with Ei = 75 meV at 6 K along the reciprocal-lattice direction (H, 0, 2). Data have been integrated in the transverse directions with K = [-0.05, 0.05] and L = [1.90, 2.10] in reciprocal lattice units (r. l. u.). For Er166, measurements were performed with Ei = 12 meV at 1.8 K along the reciprocal-lattice direction (H, 0, 2). Data have been integrated in the transverse directions with K = [-0.03, 0.03] and L = [1.80, 2.20]...

FIG. 2. Magnon chirality mixing in Er166. Half-polarized INS data for Er166 showing the magnetic contribution (σM) (a)–(b) and the chiral contribution (c)–(d) to spin excitations along the reciprocal-lattice direction (H, 0, 0) and (1, 0, L), respectively. The scattering events were collected with Ei = 15 meV at 6 K. The gray solid lines in (a) correspond to the model dispersion. (e), (f) Model calculations of the chiral scattering along the two directions convoluted with a Gaussian energy full-width-at-half-maximum of 0.4 meV. The gray shaded regions in (a-d) are obscured by the kinematic limit.

FIG. 3. Magnon spin angular momentum. Sublattice SAM and total SAM (in units of ℏ) for acoustic and optic modes in (a), (b) Tb166 and (c), (d) Er166. In each panel, the lower plot shows the sublattice weight for each eigenvector. Thin vertical lines indicate the wavevector where the modes cross.

FIG. 4. Magnon mode eigenvectors. Precession of rare- earth moments (orange arrow) and Mn moments (green ar- row) in a right-handed (red cone) or left-handed fashion (blue cone) relative to the net magnetization (M). Eigenvectors are shown near the mode-crossing wavevector for (a) Tb166 and (b) Er166. For Er166, the Er and Mn moments precess with opposite handedness, allowing the cancellation of the net SAM and chirality.
